Drag to turn, pinch or scroll to zoom. Tap a cube to jump to its move. Drag the slider to go through the plan by hand. On a keyboard, space plays and the arrow keys step. Moves in order

    Run log: score a real run

    A score sheet for practice with the real claw. It counts how many moves worked and times each one, so the notebook gets real numbers.

    1. Set the real cubes up like the start card. Tap Start a run. That starts the clock.
    2. Do the move named below with the real claw.
    3. Tap how it went. The page saves the result and the seconds it took, then shows the next move.
    4. When the card is built, copy the log into the notebook's test table.

    Good: the cube got to its spot. Dropped: the claw lost it. Bumped: it knocked another cube.

    REEKON tape bench

    Our REEKON digital tape types its measurements straight into this page. Put the tape in Keyboard Mode with Enter as the ending and connect it over Bluetooth. Then every press of save lands in the box that is lit up. Typing by hand works too.

    1. Does the real stand match the CAD?

    Ten sizes of the stand. The drawing shows where the tape starts (1) and where to read it (2). Start measuring walks through all ten, one at a time.

    The green line on the 3D stand in the Plan tab shows the same thing.

    3. Cube sizes (test T0)

    Tap the box, then measure every cube across, from one flat face to the opposite face. Each save adds one, with how far the closed claw would squeeze it in on each side.

      4. Tests by tape


        5. Drive by tape

        The stand has no sensor for where it is along the row, so the tape does that job. Before every grab and every set-down, the page says what the tape should read from the zero mark to the middle of the stand. When it reads right, the plan steps on and the move goes into the run log with how far off the stand was.

        6. Lines and marks, from the CAD

          All 132 pairs

          Fewest moves for every start and end card, with the rules set above.

          Front is the side you see on the printed card. Every move is checked against our claw and stand, with sizes from the CAD. All three claws give the same plans, because they all hang from P05 with 70 mm blades: a taller cube against a gripped face, the bar, and the 2x4 base all have to clear. The check does not cover park spots or the path while carrying. Cards typed from the game cards PDF on Nov 15, 2026.
